en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Eighth Chapter
The Discussion on the Bases in the Realm of Form:
Is there a personal existence consisting of the six bases in the realm of form?
Yes, [it is] so.
Is there the sense-base of the nose there? Yes.
Is there the sense-base of odors there?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is there the sense-sphere of the tongue there? Yes.
Is there the taste-base (rasāyatana) therein?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Is there the body-base (kāyāyatana) therein?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is there, then, the tangible base (*phoṭṭhabbāyatana*) therein?
You should not speak thus… [and so on]…
Is there no sense-sphere of odor there?
Yes. Is there no sense-sphere of nose there? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is there no sense-sphere of taste there? Yes.
Is there no tongue-base there?
It should not be said so … pe … Is there no tangible-object-base there?
“Yes,” you say.
“Is there no body-base (kāyāyatana) there?
You should not say so… [and so on]… No, indeed.
Is there the eye-base there, and is there the visible-object-base there?
Yes. Is there the nose-base there, and is there the odor-base there?
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is there,
in that case, the eye-base and the visible-object-base? Yes.
Is there there the tongue-base, is there the taste-base?
…pe… Is there there the body-base, is there the tangible-base?
One should not say so …pe…
Is there there the sense-base of the ear, is there the sense-base of sound …pe… is there there the sense-base of the mind,
is there the sense-base of mental phenomena? Yes.
Is there the nose-base there, and is there the odor-base there?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Is there the mind-base there, and is there the mental-object-base there?
“Yes,” he replied.
“In that [state], is there the tongue-base and the taste-base?
…pe… Is there the body-base and the tangible-object-base?”
It should not be said thus... [etc.
...Is it the case that the nose-base exists there, but the odor-base does not? Yes.
Is it the case that the eye-base exists there, but the visible-form base does not?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Is it the case that the nose-base exists there, but the odor-base does not?
“Yes.
“Is there, in that case, the sense-base of the ear, but not the sense-base of sounds?
…pe… Is there, in that case, the sense-base of the mind, but not the sense-base of mental objects?”
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is there the tongue-base there,
but no taste-base … [as before] … Is there the body-base there, but no tangible-object-base?
“Yes,” [you say].
“In that case, does the eye-base exist there, but the visible-object-base not exist?
You should not speak thus … [and so on] …
Is there the body-base there, but no tangible-object-base?
Yes. Is there the ear-base there, but no sound-base? ... [and so on] ... Yes.
Is there the sense-base of mind there, but no sense-base of mental phenomena?
You should not say so… [as before] … Is there the sense-base of the eye there and the sense-base of visible forms there, and does one see that visible form with that eye?
“Yes,” [you say].
“In that case, there is the nose-base and there is the odor-base; does one smell that odor with that nose?
You should not speak thus …pe…
Is there there the eye-base and the form-base, such that by means of that eye one sees that form?
Yes. Is there there the tongue-base and the taste-base, such that by means of that tongue one tastes that taste? ... [and so on] ... Yes.
Is there there the body-base and the tangible-object-base, such that one touches that tangible object with that body?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Is there there the ear-base and the sound-base... [and so on]?
Is there there the mind-base and the mental-object-base; and by means of that mind, does one cognize that mental object?
Yes. Is there there the nose-base and the odor-base; and by means of that nose, does one smell that odor?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Therein exists the mind-base (manāyatana) and there exists the mental-object-base (dhammāyatana); does one cognize that mental object with that mind? Yes.
"There is there the tongue-base and there is the taste-base...
[and so on] ...there is there the body-base and there is the tangible-object-base; does one touch that tangible object with that body?
One should not say so... [and so on].
Is there the nose-base there and the odor-base there, yet one does not smell that odor with that nose? Yes.
Is there the eye-base there and the visible-form-base there, yet one does not see that visible form with that eye?
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is it the case that there is the nose-base there and there is the odor-base there, yet one does not smell that odor with that nose? Yes.
Is there there the sense-base of the ear and the sense-base of sounds ... pe ...
is there there the sense-base of the mind and the sense-base of mental objects, yet one does not cognize that mental object with that mind?
One should certainly not say so ... pe ... .
Is there there the tongue-base and the taste-base …pe… is there there the body-base and the tangible-object-base, yet one does not touch that tangible object with that body? Yes.
Is there there the sense-base of the ear, is there the sense-base of sounds …pe… is there there the sense-base of the mind,
is there the sense-base of mental phenomena, yet one does not cognize that mental phenomenon with that mind?
One should certainly not say so …pe…
Is there there the nose-base and the odor-base, such that one smells that odor with that nose? Yes.
Are there there root-odors, heartwood-odors, bark-odors, leaf-odors, flower-odors, fruit-odors, raw-odors, putrid-odors, pleasant odors, and unpleasant odors?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is there the tongue-base there, is there the taste-base there, and does one taste that taste with that tongue? Yes.

Is there there the taste of roots, the taste of stems, the taste of bark, the taste of leaves, the taste of flowers, or the taste of fruits; is there sour, sweet, bitter, pungent, salty, alkaline, astringent, astringent-sour, astringent-bitter, pleasant, or unpleasant?
You should not say so… [as before]… Is there there the body-base (kāyāyatana) and the tangible-object-base (phoṭṭhabbāyatana), such that one touches that tangible object with that body?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is there therein what is hard, soft, smooth, rough, pleasant contact, painful contact, heavy, and light?
You should not speak thus … [as before] … .
Is it not to be said that the personal existence consisting of the six sense bases exists in the realm of form?
Yes, it is.
Is it not the case that there is there the sign of the nose, the sign of the tongue, and the sign of the body?
Yes, it is so.
Since there is there the sign of the nose, the sign of the tongue, and the sign of the body, then indeed, O sir, you must say this:
“The personal existence consisting of the six sense bases exists in the form element.
The discussion on the sense bases in the form element is finished.
